question: What changes if diets are compared only on the day-21 weight, instead of on the whole growth trajectory?
claim: Day-21 weight by diet, in 45 of 50 chicks
n_observations: none; each of the 45 points is one chick's day-21 weight
error_bar: mean with 95% CI, computed per diet over the chicks drawn in that diet (the n printed above it)

y.note: points, not bars, so a non-zero baseline is permitted (A2); the drawn range 59-388 g spans every displayed chick (74-373 g)

color.redundant_with: x position and x tick label

excluded: 5 of 50 chicks were never weighed on day 21 and are not drawn; the loss is unequal across the diets being compared (diet 1: 4 of 20; diet 2: 0 of 10; diet 3: 0 of 10; diet 4: 1 of 10), and retained/assigned is printed under every diet on the figure
missing: none among the 45 displayed chicks: each has all 12 scheduled weighings and every point is an observed day-21 measurement, none interpolated or imputed
_notes: On the excluded chicks: they were last weighed on days 2-20 at 35-146 g. Those are earlier-day weights, not day-21 weights, so they are not comparable to the plotted values and are not drawn; for scale, 6 of the 45 displayed day-21 weights fall below the largest of them, and the displayed weights span 74-373 g. The direction of the loss therefore cannot be read off this figure; it is visible in the trajectories of step 21. What this figure does show is that diet 1 contributes 4 fewer chicks to the comparison than it was assigned, while diets 2, 3 lose none.
